question.problem: Expressed as an improper fraction in its lowest terms, $6÷\frac{8}{11}=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Dividing a whole number by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying the whole number by the reciprocal of the fraction.

First, we write $6$ as an improper fraction:

$$
6=\frac{6}{1}
$$

Next, we note that the reciprocal of $\frac{8}{11}$ is $\frac{11}{8}.$ 

So, we have

$$
6÷\frac{8}{11}=\frac{6}{1}÷\frac{8}{11}=\frac{6}{1}\times \frac{11}{8}.
$$

 

Now, we multiply our fractions. Note that we can simplify the process by swapping the denominators first.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{1}\times \frac{11}{8} & =\frac{6}{8}\times \frac{11}{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\times 11 \\  & =\frac{33}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
